subject: Literature
title: Salman Rushdie's The Satanic Verses
description: A micro-lesson that makes Salman Rushdie's The Satanic Verses usable.

hook.text: In 1989, Iran's Ayatollah Khomeini issued a fatwa calling for the death of novelist Salman Rushdie.

buildup.text: The Satanic Verses was accused of blasphemy against Islam, and Rushdie was forced into hiding for over a decade.

discovery.text: The novel is actually a complex exploration of migration, identity, and faith, not a simple attack on religion.

twist.text: In 2022, Rushdie was stabbed on stage in New York, showing the fatwa's violence had not ended after thirty years.

climax.text: The Rushdie affair forced the world to confront the conflict between free expression and religious sensitivities.

punchline.text: A novel about faith became a test of freedom itself.

quiz.question: What happened to Rushdie decades after the fatwa was issued?
options: He was formally pardoned by Iran
He was stabbed on stage in New York in 2022
